layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract. Accurately segmenting thin tubular structures, such as ves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sels, nerves, roads or concrete cracks, is a crucial task in computer vi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion. Standard deep learning-based segmentation loss functions, such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dice or Cross-Entropy, focus on volumetric overlap, often at the ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pense of preserving structural connectivity or topology. This can lead

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to segmentation errors that adversely affect downstream tasks, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flow calculation, navigation, and structural inspection. Although current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology-focused losses mark an improvement, they introduce significant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational and memory overheads. This is particularly relevant for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3D data, rendering these losses infeasible for larger volumes as well as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasingly important multi-class segmentation problems. To mitigate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this, we propose a novel Skeleton Recall Loss, which effectively addresses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these challenges by circumventing intensive GPU-based calculations with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inexpensive CPU operations. It demonstrates overall superior perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance to current state-of-the-art approaches on five public datasets for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology-preserving segmentation, while substantially reducing compu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tational overheads by more than 90%. In doing so, we introduce the

layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The precise segmentation of thin tubular structures is a critical task across di-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: verse domains in engineering and medical applications (Fig. 1). Topological cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rectness is fundamental for facilitating downstream tasks such as analyzing blood

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flow dynamics, delineating neuronal boundaries in Electron Microscopy imagery

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluating risk factors for vascular pathologies, aiding in surgical planning, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimizing route planning [1, 5, 6, 21, 32, 40]. Classical approaches for the auto-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mated segmentation of thin curvilinear structures have encompassed methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including image transforms [25, 34], mathematical morphologies [29, 41], filter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing [10,13,15], differential operators [33], among others [2,3,8,16,19]. Deep learn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing based techniques have played an increasing role in recent years with standard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation networks such as UNet [27] being popular. Standard overlap-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: losses (eg. dice-similarity coefficient [43) enable such networks to segment large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures while often struggling with small elongated ones [18] as shown in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 2.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Multiple methods have been introduced in recent years to address the chal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lenges of segmenting thin curvilinear structures but are often domain-specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or require the use of specialized networks [4, 9, 17, 22–24, 39]. Recently, center-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lineDice [31] (clDice) was introduced encompassing both a loss function and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a metric for measuring connectivity in segmentation of thin structures. Effec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tively, it incorporates the skeleton of a segmentation into the dice calculation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While the clDice metric uses the exact skeleton, the clDice loss works with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differentiable approximation of the skeleton. It is used to enable architecture-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: independent, topology-aware segmentation of thin tubular structures and is con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sidered as state-of-the art. However, despite its advantages, it introduces a large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational overhead. Furthermore, the differentiable Soft Skeleton used in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the loss calculation can often be jagged as depicted in Fig. 3, leading to inac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curacies in segmentation. While a follow-up approach [20] attempted to address

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this limitation by introducing a topological-correct differentiable skeleton, it did

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: so while being even more computationally expensive. This limitation becomes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly pronounced when dealing with large volumes or multi-class segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation problems common to 3D medical image segmentation, rendering training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on multi-class 3D datasets challenging to infeasible even on modern hardware.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In response to these challenges, we propose Skeleton Recall Loss, a novel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loss function tailored to address the intricacies associated with thin structures in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks. Skeleton Recall Loss demonstrates the following strengths:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Minimal training time: The Tubed Skeleton required by Skeleton Recall

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Loss can be computed with simple CPU-based operations using common

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image processing frameworks (e.g. scikit-image [38]) as part of data-loading

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or even be precomputed. It is then used in a simple additional soft recall loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the prediction, thus requiring very little additional training time.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Minimal training memory: The utilization of Skeleton Recall Loss entails

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: minimal GPU Memory overhead. Unlike approaches reliant on a differen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tiable skeleton in prediction or ground truth during training, Skeleton Recall

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Loss sidesteps the computationally taxing GPU-based skeletonization pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cess, thus necessitating only a marginal increase in GPU training memory.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Domain and architecture agnostic: Skeleton Recall Loss exhibits inher-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ent plug-and-play characteristics, seamlessly integrating into a wide array of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2D and 3D segmentation tasks without imposing architectural constraints.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It operates without the need for specialized networks or modifications to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: underlying segmentation architectures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Multi-class compatibility: Skeleton Recall Loss integrates seamlessly with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-class labels, while competing methods like clDice Loss, often face near

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: insurmountable computational challenges on such problems.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Skeleton Recall Loss yields overall superior results to a baseline network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without topological losses, as well as against clDice Loss as a state-of-the-art

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topological loss. We demonstrate this effectiveness on extensive multi-domain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation on 5 publicly available datasets. Notably, our loss function inherently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feasibly supports multi-class segmentation problems and thus can be considered

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a new state-of-the-art for dilineating thin curvilinear structures in natural as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as medical images.

layout_dets.text: learn features as well as global topology. Also, in [17], a pair of sequential UN-

layout_dets.text: 3 Methodology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1 The challenges of Differentiable Skeletons

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The usage of a differentiable skeleton based loss [20, 28, 31, 37] in training a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deep neural network to segment thin tubular structures is an intuitive approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to preserve connectivity. However, it is fraught with challenges which can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-faceted in nature. One of the most easily demonstrable issues is shown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Fig. 3. As mentioned earlier, the so-called Soft skeletonization of clDice Loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can lead to perforated and jagged skeletons, especially in 3D, which results in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inaccuracies for the clDice Loss calculation. This is in addition to the enormous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: GPU memory and training time overheads that are a natural part of a GPU-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based differentiable skeletonization process on both the ground truth as well as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the network prediction. This overhead is demonstrated in Fig. 7, and can render

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effective training almost infeasible in multi-class datasets with large 3D input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volumes such as TopCoW [40] (which is used in this work) without access to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significant computational resources. While follow-up work in [20] allowed for a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relative improvement in topologically accurate differentiable skeletonization, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further aggravated the issues with excessive resource utilization.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2 Skeleton Recall Loss: Connectivity conservation on thin

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures without differentiable skeletons

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Skeleton Recall Loss is a loss function designed to preserve connectivity in thin

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tubular structures without incurring massive computational overheads. It is uni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: versally applicable, regardless of whether the inputs are 2D or 3D. It does so by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Instead, a tubed skeletonization is performed on the ground truth, followed by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a soft recall loss against the predicted segmentation output. This is illustrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Fig. 4 and further discussed in the following sections.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tubed Skeletonization The usage of a skeleton for the preservation of con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nectivity is an effective method, but it does not need to be differentiable. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this work, we extract a tubed skeleton from the ground truth as demonstrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Algorithm 1. Initially, we binarize the ground truth segmentation mask and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compute its skeleton using methods outlined in [42] for 2D and [14] for 3D inputs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Subsequently, we dilate the skeleton with a diamond kernel of radius 2 to make it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tubular, thereby enlarging the effective area for loss computation around the oth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erwise thin, single-pixel-wide skeleton. This enhances the stability of the loss by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incorporating signals from a greater number of pixels, particularly those in close

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proximity to the skeleton, which are vital for connectivity. Lastly, for multi-class

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problems, we multiply the tubed skeleton with the ground truth mask, effectively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assigning parts of the skeleton to their respective classes. All of these operations

layout_dets.text: 4.2 Evaluation Metrics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We use multiple metrics including overlap, connectivity and topological measures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for thorough evaluation of our proposed loss function. An interesting dichotomy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of clDice [31] is that while it makes for an inefficient loss function for training deep

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neural networks, it is an effective metric for measuring connectivity. Therefore,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: following existing guidelines [18] for semantic segmentation of tubular structures,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we use clDice as a metric in conjunction with Dice similarity coefficient, as our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connectivity- and overlap-based measures. Similar to previous work, we also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: report on topology-based metrics, namely, absolute Betti Number Errors of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Betti Numbers,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . However, in contrast to other work [11,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 31], we calculate the Betti Errors on whole volumes instead of small, randomly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extracted patches. Our evaluation strategy is more intuitive in nature and offers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: better interpretability of the measure, which is especially relevant in medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.text: it infeasible on all 13 classes as it exceeded the memory capacity of an A100

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 40GB GPU. In summary, Skeleton Recall Loss can be employed for an arbitrary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: number of classes with minimal computational cost.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6 Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This paper proposes a novel loss function, Skeleton Recall Loss, designed for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connectivity preserving semantic segmentation. It is domain and architecture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: agnostic and, unlike existing methods, requires minimal additional training time

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and memory. Through extensive evaluation on five publicly available datasets,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we demonstrate that Skeleton Recall Loss shows overall superior performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on existing state-of-the-art topology-aware loss functions. Moreover, it stands

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the first loss function designed for computationally manageable thin struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture segmentation within the increasingly significant but hitherto unaddressed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-class context. In essence, Skeleton Recall Loss represents a significant ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vancement in the field of thin structure segmentation, offering both efficiency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and efficacy. The public availability of our code further facilitates its adoption

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and serves as a foundation for future advancements in this critical area of study.
